7. The trial Court examined 9(nine) PWs and they have been cross-examined by the defence. Thereafter, on an application, the learned Special Judge on 19.05.2020 granted bail to accused-respondent No.1 whereupon the present petitioner (Durnity Daman Commission) being aggrieved filed revisional application under section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 being Virtual Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.91 of 2020 before the High Court Division who after hearing the parties on 28.05.2020 stayed the bail granting order of the Special Judge dated 19.05.2020. 

 11. Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner, submits that section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 deals with appeal, revision and transfer of cases. Section 10(1) and (1A) of the Act, 1958 runs as follows: 

 12. Mr. Alam further submits that in view of section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, the revisional application before the High Court Division is maintainable in the eye of law and that there is no legal bar for taking the recourse of law against the judgment and order passed by the Special Judge, but the High Court Division failed to appreciate the same. He further submits that though the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2012 is a special law but the trial has been conducted under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and as such, question of availing the jurisdiction under section 10(1 A) of the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1958 is very much applicable in the eye of law, but the High Court Division failed to appreciate the same. He further submits that the impugned order of bail passed by the Special Judge, Court No. 6, Dhaka is bad in law as well as facts and as such, the judgment and order passed by the Virtual Division Bench of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. He also submits that the High Court Division without touching the merit of the case discharged the Rule on the ground of maintainability which is an error in the impugned decision and thus interference is called for by this Division. He further submits that the order of bail passed by the trial Court is contrary to the judgment of the High Court Division in the case of Rashedul Huq Chishti vs The State and another, reported in 24 BLC (HD) (2019) 48 and as such, the judgment and order passed by the Virtual Division Bench of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. He also submits that at the trial 9 (nine) PWs have already been examined and they have been cross-examined by the defence at the midst of trial, question of bail does not arise at all and as such, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. He lastly submits that the case relates to financial crime and laundered of taka more than 159 crore but the trial Court without considering the vital aspect of the case most illegally granted bail to 'accused-respondent No.1 and as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. 

 17. The High Court Division in the impugned judgment opines that the instant revision filed under section 10(1A)of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 is not maintainable regarding accepting bail under মানিলন্ডারিং প্রতিরোধ আইন, ২০১২  (Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012) since section মানিলন্ডারিং প্রতিরোধ আইন, ২০১২, (Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012) particularly mention the provision of preferring appeal against the judgment and/or order passed by the Special Judge with regard to money laundering offences. 

 19. On the other hand, section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 provides- 

 20. From the above bare text of the provisions, it is apparent that section 22 of the Act of 2012 only provides the window of appeal whereas section 10(1 A) of the Act of 1958 provides the procedure of revision. 

 25. Now, let us see whether section 22 of the Act of 2012 is contrary to section 10(1A) of the Act of 1958? 

 26. Section 3 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958 created the post of Special Judge wherein it has been also enacted that from the time being in charge of the trial of the offences under মানিলন্ডারিং প্রতিরোধ আইন, ২০১২, (Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012). Though section 10 of the মানিলন্ডারিং প্রতিরোধ আইন, ২০১২ (Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012) authorizes the Special Judge to hold the trial, however, schedule of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 has been amended for this very purpose. In the case of money laundering, these two Acts are not contrary but auxiliary. Money Laundering Prevention Act adopts the Special Judge as its curator. On the other hand, the Criminal Law Amendment Act provides the fact of creation of a post of Special Judge. The inherent law for Special Judge, i.e. the Criminal Law Amendment Act provides, in its section 10(1A), that the High Court Division shall also have powers of revisions against the judgment of a Special Judge. This pristine authority of the High Court Division cannot be taken away without amending the very same Act. As a result, we are of the view that section 22 of the Act of 2012 is not contrary to section 10(1A) of the Act of 1958, as well as does not curtail the power of revision of the High Court Division, rather provides an additional jurisdiction of institution of appeal in addition to prefer a revision. 

 27. From the above discussion, this Division holds the view that a revision under section 10(1A) of the Act of 1958 against an order of the Special Judge is quite maintainable and alternatively there opened a new avenue of preferring an appeal under section 22 of the Money Laundering Prevention Act of 2012.
